accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute: a dispute over the sale of property, with the deceased acting as the property dealer
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 and s.304 read with s.34
weapon: Revolver (.32 bore Smith & Wesson), fired at the deceased; the weapon used by the appellant could not be determined by ballistics
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony (conflicting versions), medical evidence on range of shot, ballistic and recovery evidence
mitigating_circumstances: Sudden fight in heat of passion; shot fired in private defence after being strangled; no premeditation; no undue advantage taken
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC ss.302 and 304 r/w s.34 for the deaths of both brothers; sentence not stated in the judgment
high_court_outcome: High Court judgment dated 01.09.2010 (Crl. A. 232/1997) was impugned before the Supreme Court; the State's appeal (Crl. A. 226/1997) seeking death penalty was dismissed
offence_finally_established: IPC s.304 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) for the death of Shyam Sunder
neutral_facts: The incident occurred in the afternoon at the office of a third person, which had been arranged as a meeting to settle a dispute over the sale of a property, through a property dealer, between the accused and one of the victims. The victim, his two brothers and a witness were already present when the accused arrived with his father and another man. Witnesses gave two versions of what followed. One witness said that as soon as the deceased got up, the accused took out a revolver and fired at him, after which the accused's father also fired at the victim's brothers. Another witness said that the three brothers and the accused were involved in a scuffle in which the deceased and his brothers tried to strangulate the accused. The accused then reached for his revolver, the deceased released him and turned to run, and the accused fired. The bullet entered below the right shoulder of the deceased from the back and did not exit. A doctor stated that the shot was fired from a distant range, with no blackening, tattooing or charring. Seven bullets were fired and no empty cartridge cases were found at the scene. Two .32 revolvers were recovered, one from the accused and one from his father, but ballistic examination could not link the bullets to the accused's revolver. Two brothers died from gunshot wounds and a third brother was injured. Several witnesses gave differing accounts of who fired which shot.
physical_harm: Death of two brothers by gunshot (one shot in the back below the right shoulder; three .32 bullets recovered from Kishan Lal's body); a third brother was injured by bullets
number_of_offences: 2 charged (IPC s.302 and s.304 r/w s.34); 1 finally upheld (s.304)
premeditation_planning: No premeditation found; homicide was the result of a sudden fight in heat of passion, relying on the Sessions Court and High Court findings
motive: alleged: dispute over the sale of a property arranged through the deceased as property dealer
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of PW-23 and PW-27 on the scuffle; medical evidence that the shot was fired from a distant range; the bullet's entry and upward trajectory without exit; ballistic report
witness_credibility: PW-3 and PW-30 rejected on the no-scuffle version (PW-30's account inconsistent with the wound position); PW-27's testimony unshaken in cross-examination and accepted; PW-23 accepted on scuffle; PW-3 not credible on who fired at Kishan Lal
post_offence_conduct: Per the prosecution account (not a court finding): the accused and his father fled the place in another visitor's car
custody_duration: Approximately 13½ years of sentence undergone as on the date of judgment; the appellant is in jail
trial_duration: offence: 04.03.1991; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 01.09.2010; Supreme Court: February 02, 2017
legal_representation: Appellant: Sushil Kumar and S. K. Aggarwal (Sr. Advs.) with others; State: P. K. Dey and others
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under ss.302 and 304 r/w s.34. High Court: judgment dated 01.09.2010 under challenge (Crl. A. 232/1997). Supreme Court: appeal partly allowed; s.302 conviction set aside for Kishan Lal's death, s.304 maintained, sentence of period already undergone
prosecution_argument: The deceased and his brothers were unarmed, so there was no need to use the gun; the appellant took undue advantage of the situation by using the gun
defence_argument: Private defence, since the accused was being strangled; alternatively, the fatal shot was fired by the father, who had a gun and wanted to protect his son
legal_principle_applied: Right of private defence under IPC s.97 and the Darshan Singh principles; Exception 2 and Exception 4 to s.300 IPC (culpable homicide not amounting to murder)
precedent_relied_upon: Darshan Singh v. State of Punjab and Another (2010) 2 SCC 333 : [2010] 1 SCR 642
sentencing_rationale: Homicide found to fall within Exception 4 to s.300 (sudden fight, no premeditation) and guilt under s.304 established; sentence set at the period already undergone. No further reasons on sentence stated.
judicial_mitigating_factors: Good-faith exercise of private defence; no premeditation; sudden fight in heat of passion; no undue advantage taken
other_sentence_order: Direction that the appellant be released forthwith from custody, if not required in any other case
